claim: *Selecting context for the work.* Standing instructions provide compact, persistent guidance. Dynamic context injection selects an initial slice of engineering knowledge at dispatch and refines that selection after planning, using a more precise account of the work. Retrieval makes relevant obligations available to the agent; separate controls are needed to enforce them.
topology: The main row runs initial agent context → agent planning → refined agent context → implementation. Engineering knowledge branches into both selections. Initial selection feeds initial context; planning supplies refined scope to refined selection, which feeds refined context. Standing instructions feed each work stage from a separate bottom bus. There is no lifecycle backedge, no planning before initial context, and no assertion that a refined slice is a superset.
bw_encoding: Only the engineering-knowledge source and standing-instructions source use light 5% gray. Selections and work-sequence stages remain white; no color implies enforcement. Engineering knowledge is bold 10.5 pt; stage and selection headings and standing-instruction heading are bold 10 pt, with Implementation bold 9.5 pt. Dispatch/planning qualifiers, refined-scope relation, and knowledge inventory are italic. Ordinary labels remain 9–9.5 pt.
redesign: Author-requested chronology redraw makes initial context, agent planning, refined context and implementation the explicit work sequence. Two selections use the same engineering knowledge. Planning supplies refined scope to the second selection, which may add or remove knowledge. Standing instructions remain available throughout; the previous lifecycle return edge is removed.
alt: The work sequence runs from initial agent context to agent planning, refined agent context, and implementation. At dispatch, an initial selection from engineering knowledge uses anticipated files and components to supply a coarse slice. After planning, the refined scope drives a second selection from the same engineering knowledge; this selection may add or remove knowledge. Engineering knowledge contains models, rules, procedures and examples. Standing instructions, consisting of mission, compact method and compact policy, remain available throughout planning and implementation. There is no lifecycle feedback loop and no implication that retrieved guidance enforces obligations.
